title: Two months ago I posted my AI-only workflow here. The demo is out now — here is what the last stretch taught me about small local models
author: DaedalusR8
selftext:
In July I posted here about building my tactical RPG, Campaign Forge, without  
writing a single line of code myself — I lead the design, review everything,  
playtest, and write picky bug reports; Claude writes all the code and all the  
docs. A few of you asked to try it. The free demo is on Steam now, and this  
sub gets the follow-up on what the final stretch was actually like.  
  
  
The code was never the problem. The project sits at just under 2,000 commits  
since March, all AI-written, and the failure modes are still the ones I  
described in July: behavioral, not syntactic. What nearly derailed the demo  
was the writing itself. The game ships with a small local language model inside it  
so campaigns generate fully offline, and the model we had bundled had a tic.  
Every chapter it wrote was full of the same figures of speech — stones that  
remember, silence that speaks, a certain "not X, it's Y" sentence shape — and  
I got to the point where I could not test my own game anymore because every  
world sounded like the same narrator.  
  
Examples include:  
"It's not growing, it's becoming"  
"It's not sleeping, it's remembering"  
"It's not something, it's nothing"  
  
The Edge of it all, I could not suffer it forever.  
  
  
My first instinct was prompts. We rewrote them positive-only, removed every  
example the model could echo, rotated the outline examples, tried lower  
temperature. It got worse. So instead of guessing we measured: Claude wrote a  
headless probe that generates a whole world plus a chapter with a given model  
and counts the tics per thousand words, then I read the prose myself. The  
result was uncomfortable and useful. The prompts were not the cause; the tic  
was the model's own prior, baked in. The bundled 4B model scored between ten  
and twenty of those per thousand words no matter what we did. A 3B  
alternative scored under five but was bland and copied our examples back at  
us. Another small model looped so badly that a quarter of its output survived  
deduplication. Gemma 3 4B came in around two per thousand, with zero  
personified nature, and its scenes were plain, concrete and coherent. We  
swapped the bundled model the same day, sorted the licence, and the chapters  
finally read like stories about the world you made instead of poems about  
stones. STONES AND TREEEEEEES AND SILENCE.  
  
  
The other lesson was on the code side of the AI seam, and I think it  
generalizes: stop asking the model to remember or to obey, and put a net  
under it instead. The model writes "it is raining" into a scene; a code-side  
net reads the scene text and turns it into actual weather on the map, with  
figurative rain of arrows excluded by shape. The model leaves a scene without  
a cast; the code casts a living resident of that region from the world  
database before it would ever invent a placeholder. The model writes a  
confrontation but forgets the person you are supposed to confront; the code  
notices and puts them in the room. Every one of those was a real bug report  
from my own playtests in the two days before release, and every fix followed  
the same pattern: the AI proposes, the code disposes, and a probe that the AI  
also wrote pins the rule so it cannot quietly regress.  
  
  
The workflow rules from July still mostly hold.  
  
  
The demo has three parts: a small hand-crafted opening chapter that plays the  
moment it loads, the world generator itself running on your PC with the  
bundled model (no account, no API key, no cloud, roughly a 3.4 GB download),  
and the boss designer we build the game with plus an arena to fight your  
creation in. Everything you forge carries into the full game when it enters  
Early Access on November 27, and we are in Steam Next Fest in October.  
  
  
Steam (the demo button is on the page): [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4918080](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4918080)  
Trailer: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7AxeDs-T0dU](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7AxeDs-T0dU)  
  
  
Happy to answer anything — how the register probe works, what "let the code  
put a net under the model" looks like in practice, which small models we  
tried and what each one did wrong, or what it is like to release a game you  
technically never know the actual Dialogue of (which is a Core part of the game).  
  
Don't judge my building interiors too harshly, I'll get there. At some point.

Assets are intended to be swappable (Asset-packs later on), to have said that.

comments.author: TottallyNotToxec
comments.body: Too lazy to get ai to format the ai description? Good sign

replies.author: DaedalusR8
replies.body:
I do use AI to enhance ALL my informational posts, I will also gladly continue doing so as I love technology and it's benefits.

If you tell me what is wrong with the formatting from your perspective, I can change it so you can better read it. I'm guessing it's a mobile issue maybe? I did not think of that before and made some adjustments now.

Thank you for your feedback, this will enhance my posts going forward.

comments.author: Proper-Zebra9264
comments.body:
Hey! Really impressive work on Campaign Forge!

I'm currently developing my own indie game in Unity, and I'm very interested in how you integrated Gemma 3 4B into your game.

I have a few questions:

1. How did you integrate Gemma 3 4B into the game? Are you using llama.cpp, Ollama, or another inference runtime?
2. Does the model run entirely offline on the player's machine, or does it require a server?
3. How do you handle the model's RAM/VRAM usage and performance on lower-end PCs?
4. Do you use a quantized version of Gemma 3 4B? If so, which one?
5. How do you connect the AI-generated content to the actual gameplay systems while keeping the game state consistent?

I'm considering implementing a similar system for NPC dialogue, memories, and dynamic events in my game.

I'd really appreciate any technical insights or advice you could share. Thanks!
